items.title: Randy Weston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My father made me take piano lessons and my mother gave me black church.

ctx.x: Were you inspired by that book and by what that book said to you when you read it? Were you inspired by that book to make this particular record as a solo piano record?

Yeah, because that book only confirms the things I had read about all my life because I had a wonderful father and mother. They were fantastic, my father and mother, you see? My father taught me to study African civilization when Africa was great. Most of us get the education of Africa, Africa after slavery, that’s where we start. My father, he already said, “Man, in my house in Brooklyn we grew up with maps of African kings and queens in the house. He’d have books written by African historians, old maps.” So, my…

Well, so many of your records have been ensembles with horns. But, in this case, you decided to make a solo piano record and I get the sense that the whole theme, “Ancient Future”, had something to do with your decision to make it a solo piano record. Was that the case?
